entities.summary: Tírechán was a 7th-century Irish bishop from north Connacht, specifically the Killala Bay area, in what is now County Mayo. He played a significant role in the Christianization of Ireland, particularly in the establishment of the monastery at Clonmacnoise. Tírechán's contributions to the development of Irish Christianity were shaped by his experiences as a missionary and his interactions with other Christian leaders of the time. The monastery at Clonmacnoise became a center of learning and culture, attracting scholars and pilgrims from across Europe. Tírechán's legacy can be seen in the numerous churches and monasteries that he founded, including the famous monastery at Clonmacnoise, which still stands today. The inscription on the Clonmacnoise High Cross, which dates back to the 10th century, bears a striking image of Tírechán, highlighting his importance in Irish history.
